A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ESC-Net study. All ten pages of each version provide readable text, equations, figures, tables, and references, supporting a reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original ESC-Net segmentation results, SAM-block and prompt-combination ablations, qualitative visualizations, and inference-time measurements in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original ESC-Net benchmark results, ablations, qualitative visualizations, and inference-time measurements in Section 4.

M1.justification: The pseudo-prompt generator, SAM blocks, vision-language fusion module, and mask decoder are unchanged. The added specification of CLIP attention-layer fine-tuning clarifies implementation already described as training the CLIP encoder in v1; it does not establish a changed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions train on COCO-Stuff and evaluate the same six benchmark variants: A-847, A-150, PC-459, PC-59, PAS-20, and PAS-20b. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same comparators within both model groups. Figure 5 still compares against CAT-Seg, and Table 4 retains ZegFormer, ZSseg, OVSeg, and CAT-Seg.

E3.justification: The stated datasets, input resolution, backbone configurations, mIoU metric, learning rates, and efficiency-measurement procedure are unchanged. The new attention-layer specification documents existing fine-tuning rather than reporting a revised experimental setting.

E4.justification: Both retain the SAM removal, random-initialization, and pretrained-block comparisons in Table 2; the prompt-combination ablations in Table 3; and the qualitative and activation-map analyses in Figures 5-6. No analytical question or supporting experiment changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without specifying repeated-run counts or seeds, uncertainty intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting practice is added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1-4 retain their numerical entries, and Figures 5-6 retain the same qualitative evidence. For example, ESC-Net with ViT-L/14 remains at 18.1 mIoU on A-847 and 27.0 on PC-459, while Table 4 still reports 0.76-second inference.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations (1)-(2) are unchanged. Equation (1) moves between pages, but no formal assumption, derivation, theorem, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about efficient one-stage SAM integration, correlation-based pseudo prompts, segmentation accuracy, and benchmark superiority. The introductory wording adjustment does not change their scientific scope.

C2.justification: The added paragraph in Section 4.3 argues that CLIP can retain linguistic discrimination when fine-tuned on datasets with limited classes, providing an explicit rationale for the training choice. The existing limitations concerning boundary precision and memory growth with class count remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v1 states that the CLIP encoder is trained; v2 specifies fine-tuning the attention layers of both image and text encoders, following CAT-Seg. This improves implementation specificity without changing the stated hyperparameters, hardware, or resource-access information.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects its attention-layer fine-tuning choice to CAT-Seg and contrasts it with earlier frozen-encoder approaches. Section 2 also removes the SAM comparison to ChatGPT and artificial general intelligence. The cited-work set remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The revision makes limited introductory and related-work edits, adds an explanatory paragraph to Section 4.3, and adds a funding acknowledgement. The main section order and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 6 is reduced from full width to one column, and Table 3 moves from the right column to the left on page 8. Text, equations, and references reflow, but all six figures and four tables retain their substantive content.

improvement.justification: Section 4.3 resolves a limited reproducibility ambiguity by identifying which CLIP layers are fine-tuned and explaining the choice through CAT-Seg. Removing the speculative SAM-AGI analogy also improves focus. Figure 6 becomes smaller and less readable, but the implementation clarification provides a modest net benefit; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
